clue.text: Straw exchanged during day following transatlantic trades

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the reshuffled straw sits inside the day

parts.note: Weds is the short form of Wednesday, a day of the week

indicators.note: letters exchanged for one another are swapped about, so the word straw is reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone swaps straw on a day spent watching goods cross the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trades' looks like commerce but means the trade winds, which blow from east to west across the Atlantic. Weds is the usual short form of Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic trade winds blow from east to west, so a ship following them sails in that direction.

clue.text: Most sage stew is cooked

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so the letters of stew and is are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe note praising stew as the wisest dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double service in the surface but here belongs to the fodder: STEW plus IS, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a synonym of wise, so the superlative most sage is the wisest.

clue.text: Include in request for help for losers

indicators.note: one piece placed in another, so the word for include sits inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal, a call for help
to include something is to add it

explanation.surface: Instructions to put losers' names into an appeal for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddos is British slang for pathetic, socially inept people, much like losers.

clue.text: Tired don starts yawning

parts.note: to don clothes is to wear them

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken from yawning

explanation.surface: A tired university don begins to yawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a university teacher; here it is the verb meaning put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary is a plain synonym for tired, describing someone worn out.

clue.text: Body of marines in formation

indicators.note: troops in formation are arranged in a new order, so the letters of marines are rearranged

explanation.surface: A body of Royal Marines drawn up in formation on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' reads as a group of troops, but it means a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Remains is a euphemism for a dead person's corpse, so a body.

clue.text: Should start to listen to unscrupulous lender

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, taken here from should

parts.note: hark is an old command meaning listen

explanation.surface: Advice that a borrower should heed warnings about a loan shark.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan shark is a moneylender charging extortionate interest, so a crook of the lending trade.

clue.text: A place to cry man occupies in pain

indicators.note: one thing occupying another fills its inside, so the cry and the man sit within the word for pain

parts.note: a sore is a painful spot
a mew is a cat's or gull's cry
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone in pain looking for a spot where a man can weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A place' looks like a noun, but the answer is an adverb; 'a place' works as an adverb too, as in 'I left it a place I forget'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere is an adverb naming an unspecified location, an indefinite spot.

clue.text: Idle fellow admitted following a statesman

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the rest is placed after the letter a
one admitted is let inside, so the comedian's first name goes into the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Eric Idle is a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.surface: A lazy man admitted to politics in the wake of a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like lazy but is Eric Idle of Monty Python.
explanation.definitionFit: Playfully, a citizen of the United States is a man of the States, hence statesman.

clue.text: No trace of pepper in Greek deep- fried dish

indicators.note: food that is fried is cooked and transformed, so the letters are rearranged
no here means without, so the trace of pepper is taken out of the next word
a trace is the smallest bit, here the first letter of pepper

explanation.surface: A recipe for a Greek deep-fried dish made without any pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No trace of pepper' takes the P from DEEP, leaving DEE; 'fried' rearranges GREEK plus DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs, eaten at British breakfasts.

clue.text: Tragically misreads guns

indicators.note: something going tragically goes badly awry, so the letters of misreads are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A misreading of the situation ends in disaster with firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are weapons worn at the side, chiefly pistols, so a kind of gun.

clue.text: Come close to heading off weak resolution

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter, here from the word for weak

parts.note: limp means weak or floppy
the end of a story is its resolution

explanation.surface: Getting near to heading off a feeble resolution before it is passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like preventing; here it beheads LIMP to IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to be about to happen, so a threat that is drawing near.

clue.text: Streams old film in Japanese, subtitled initially

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter, here of subtitled

explanation.surface: A streaming service shows an old film in Japanese with subtitles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streams' looks like a verb about online viewing; it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Jets of water or gas are forceful streams forced out of a narrow opening.

clue.text: Finally publishes file describing Conservative plot

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word publishes

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
a file is a line of people one behind another

explanation.surface: A newspaper at last publishes a dossier on a Conservative conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a conspiracy, matching the surface; here it is a story's plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyline is the sequence of events in a narrative, which is what a plot is.

clue.text: Listen to correct record

indicators.note: listening hears the sound, so the word for correct is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: right means correct

explanation.surface: An instruction to hear the right record played.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down is to record it in words.

clue.text: Murdoch could be a bit of a looker

definitions.meaning: the coloured part of the eye, a part of what looks

explanation.surface: Speculation that the novelist Murdoch was rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a looker' reads as rather good-looking; here a looker is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch is the writer; the iris is the coloured ring of the eye, so part of an organ of sight.

clue.text: Fix part involving degree of bother

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the fix and part together wrap round the degree

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly
an actor's part is a role
an MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: Fixing a part involves a certain amount of bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tiresome procedure, the sort of hassle that counts as bother.

clue.text: Call following spot of infiltration

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the call comes after the spot

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
to page someone is to call them over a speaker or pager

explanation.surface: A phone call after a spy is spotted infiltrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly working its way through a material, a gradual infiltration.

clue.text: Tolerates organs

definitions.meaning: to stomach something is to put up with it

explanation.definitionFit: Stomach as a verb means bear; as a noun it is the organ that digests food.

clue.text: Stimulate terrible singer in mid-week

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the anagram inside the middle letters
the mid part of a word is its middle letters, here of week
a terrible performance goes badly wrong, so the letters of singer are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dreadful singer is booked to liven up the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns SINGER into NERGIS, which goes 'in' EE, the middle of WEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to give vigour to, which is to stimulate.

clue.text: Drunk working inside with darkness coming

indicators.note: inside places the word for working within the word for drunk

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone drinking on the job as night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the coming evening, the night ahead, so darkness is on its way.

clue.text: Award for direction of Titanic

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to New York, where the liner was bound

explanation.surface: Speculation that the film Titanic won a prize for direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' looks like film directing; it is the compass heading of the doomed ship, to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Awards honour Broadway theatre; split as TO NY, it gives the liner's destination.

clue.text: Flat-earthers value enthusiastic new starters

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the words that follow flat

explanation.surface: Flat-earthers prize keen newcomers to their cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat-' is clipped off flat-earthers to serve as the definition, leaving earthers to start the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level or smooth, with no bumps, which is flat.

clue.text: Penguin salesman in capital retired

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the whole is read backwards
in puts the salesman inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman of Penguin books retires in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: REP goes 'in' ROME as ROREPME; 'retired' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor penguin is the largest species of penguin.

clue.text: Club suit is not working as a tactic

parts.note: to club someone is to strike them
a lawsuit is a legal action

explanation.surface: A club's suit fails as a tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' and 'suit' tempt toward playing cards; both are verbs or legal terms here.
explanation.definitionFit: Strike action is a stoppage by workers who refuse to work as a bargaining tactic.

clue.text: See 21
Girl brought back in air-ambulance

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters are read in reverse
in shows the letters sit inside the words air-ambulance

explanation.surface: A girl is flown home in an air ambulance.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a girl's name, as in West Side Story or The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Mix a bit of pilau rice with hint of kidneys

indicators.note: mixing stirs ingredients together, so the letters are rearranged
a bit of a word here is its first letter, from pilau

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: stir pilau rice with a hint of kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' shuffles P (a bit of pilau) with RICE and HINT; 'hint' looks like a seasoning amount but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephritic is the medical adjective for things relating to the kidneys or to nephritis.

clue.text: Plays loudly in orgies regularly

indicators.note: in sets the loud mark within the letters taken from orgies
regularly takes every other letter of orgies

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Music played loudly at regular orgies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' stands for ff, the musical marking fortissimo, which goes 'in' the letters that 'regularly' takes from orgies.
explanation.definitionFit: To riff is to play a short repeated musical phrase, as a guitarist plays.

clue.text: Pants from touch in osculation

indicators.note: from shows the answer is drawn out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Trousers coming off during a passionate kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'osculation' is a formal word for kissing, so the surface is about touching while kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinos are cotton twill trousers, and pants is the American word for trousers.

clue.text: The writing's on the wall for vandals

definitions.text: The writing's on the wall for vandals

parts.words: The writing's on the wall for vandals
parts.note: the idiom for impending doom read literally: the words vandals spray on walls

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'the writing's on the wall' means doom is near; read literally, vandals' writing on walls is graffiti.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are words or images scrawled or sprayed on public walls, typically by vandals.

clue.text: Upset at setting part of play in field

definitions.meaning: making a ... is a noisy upset or fuss
a play is divided into acts and ...
a ... is a field of activity, as the music ...

explanation.surface: Upset at the staging of part of a play outdoors in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Scene covers a public fuss, a location, a subdivision of a play and a sphere of activity.

clue.text: Composer has problem with fringe benefits but not detailed effigy

indicators.note: a problem with something knocks it into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
detailed means with its tail cut off, so effigy loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A composer has trouble with perks, though no carefully crafted statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes EFFIG (EFFIGY 'detailed') from the letters of FRINGE BENEFITS; 'problem with' rearranges the remaining RNEBENITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was the American composer of West Side Story.
